The root `License` file (capital L, lowercase rest — that casing is why a naive LICENSE probe 404s) reads: 'Remix Icon License v1.0 / Version 1.0 - January 2026 / Copyright (c) 2017-2026 Remix Design'. I checked the file's commit history via the atom feed: it was replaced on 2026-01-25. I then downloaded the published remixicon-4.9.1.tgz (published 2026-01-29, FOUR DAYS AFTER the relicense) and extracted package/License — it ships the new restrictive license while package.json still declares "license":"Apache-2.0". The npm metadata is simply stale/wrong. Corroborated by GitHub issue #1069 'License Change Notice' and web reporting of the 2026-01-25 change.
verified.integration_notes: The new terms are NOT OSI-permissive. Section 3.1 prohibits distributing the Icons as a standalone product, icon pack, icon library, or 'downloadable asset collection where the Icons themselves constitute the primary product value'. Section 3.2 prohibits using the Icons to 'create, distribute, or sell a competing icon library or icon set, even if modified with only minor or superficial changes'. Section 3.3 prohibits logo/trademark/brand-identity use. Attribution is optional (that part loosened). WHY THIS BITES EXELMJ SPECIFICALLY: EXELMJ is a design tool that would ship a browsable, searchable, recolorable icon picker and let users stamp and MODIFY icons and export them. Section 3.2's 'even if modified with only minor changes (color, size, stroke width, corner radius, layout)' describes an icon panel in a vector editor almost verbatim. That ambiguity is precisely what a permissive-only constraint exists to avoid. ESCAPE HATCH (documented, not recommended): remixicon@4.8.0 and earlier were released under Apache-2.0, and Apache-2.0 grants are irrevocable for copies already received — @iconify-json/ri@1.2.10's info.json still records icon-set version 4.8.0 with spdx 'Apache-2.0', so that snapshot predates the change. But pinning a frozen pre-relicense fork forever is a maintenance liability and invites a version-drift accident. SECOND-ORDER WARNING: Iconify's per-set license metadata has not caught up either, so any tooling that trusts info.json will keep reporting Apache-2.0 for `ri`. Do not let that reassure you.
verified.reason: Relicensed 2026-01-25 from Apache-2.0 to a bespoke license with competing-library, standalone-distribution, and brand-use restrictions — and the npm package still falsely declares Apache-2.0. Fails the permissive-only constraint, and the competing-library clause points directly at what a design tool with an icon browser does. Use Tabler (plain MIT) instead.
